Harry Bush was an English cricketer born on January 23, 1910, in Chichester, Sussex. He played as a right-handed batsman and was known for his contributions to the game primarily during the 1930s. Bush made his first-class debut for Sussex in 1932 and had a career that spanned until 1939. 

Throughout his career, Bush played in a number of matches, showcasing his batting skills in the competitive rounds of county cricket. He was part of the Sussex team in an era when the county was not as dominant as in other periods, but he played alongside and against some notable players of his time.

After retiring from playing, Bush's contributions to cricket continued, although detailed records of his post-playing career are not as prominently noted. His life and career were often marked by the larger context of the sport during the interwar years and the significance of Sussex as a cricketing county.

Harry Bush passed away on July 6, 1988. His legacy, like that of many cricketers from his era, contributes to the rich history of English cricket.
